test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 10 Sept, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A bronze article having a marked price of ₹1,000 is sold during a festive season sale after three successive discounts of 20% and 30% and 10%. What will be the amount (in ₹) to be paid by a customer if she buys the article during the festival season?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Successive discounts act as successive multiplying factors on the marked price.

SP = MP × (1 − 0.20) × (1 − 0.30) × (1 − 0.10)

SP = 1000 × 0.8 × 0.7 × 0.9

SP = 1000 × 0.504 = 504

**∴ The correct answer is ₹504.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹1,000

Successive discounts = 20%, 30%, and 10%

**Formula Used:**

SP = MP × (100 − D₁)/100 × (100 − D₂)/100 × (100 − D₃)/100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7445081bb0b6fc18e91cfcf6ab5ae46ef4ed8ed17d09a6af5315f8c15e34065d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Discount 1 = 20% of 1000 = ₹200

⇒ Price after 1st discount = 1000 − 200 = ₹800

⇒ Discount 2 = 30% of 800 = ₹240

⇒ Price after 2nd discount = 800 − 240 = ₹560

⇒ Discount 3 = 10% of 560 = ₹56

⇒ Final Selling Price = 560 − 56 = ₹504

**∴ The correct answer is ₹504.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Equivalent Discount Formula

For two successive discounts of x% and y%, the equivalent single discount is given by (x + y − xy/100)%.

Base for Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP), never on the Cost Price (CP). Selling Price is calculated as MP − Discount.

Successive Discounts Concept

When multiple discounts are offered, each subsequent discount is calculated on the reduced price from the previous step, not on the original Marked Price.
